etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Late 16th century, from earlier heyda (1520s), as exclamation; compare hey, hei and Swedish hej då. Sense “period of success, vigor” is a reanalysis as heyday based on unrelated day (as “period of time”) – compare day in the sun.
senses: A period of success, popularity, or power; prime.
(archaic) An exultation of the spirits; gaiety; frolic.
(obsolete) An expression of frolic and exultation, and sometimes of wonder.
